cue_position: The review classified most self-report items as HIGH or MODERATE cue after revision, and none as LOW. Wording cannot eliminate social desirability and this pack does not claim it does. The objective was to reduce obviousness, not to make the self-report objective. A HIGH-CUE item is not a blocker while it is presented explicitly as self-description; it is recorded here for pilot analysis.
product_boundary: Self-report shows how the candidate describes their own working style and behavioural patterns. It is candidate self-description, useful for human review and for structured interview follow-up. It is NOT observed evidence, proof of competence, evidence maturity, suitability, a personality diagnosis or an employment recommendation. No single self-report item may independently establish a competency; self_report carries counts_toward_maturity = false, so no self-report answer can move a measured evidence level.
pilot_watch: Ceiling effects: the share of candidates choosing the top scale point on each of the 20 frequency items, per item and overall.
Socially desirable extremes: candidates whose answers sit at the desirable end on nearly every item, and whether those runs differ from the rest.
Item completion time: time per self-report item, and whether the revised stems (c08, c11, c13, c15, c17, c23) read slower than the unchanged ones.
Experience-level differences: response distributions for candidates with and without previous guarding employment, on the four generalised items (c09, c12, c20, c21) in particular.
c07 and c19 response distribution: whether the non-monotonic keys describe anything the distribution supports, which is the evidence a future keying review needs.
Forced-choice behaviour on c03, c06, c18 and c24: split, and whether either option is effectively never chosen.
SV/EN response patterns: whether the same item behaves differently in the two languages, which would point at the still-outstanding named human language review.
Non-response and change-of-answer rates per item, as a read on whether a stem is being understood.
not_claimed: No psychometric threshold, reliability coefficient, validity claim, norm or empirical difficulty is asserted by this review.
The named human language gate remains open; the English adaptation is marked adaptation_reviewed, which is not approved.
All 250 review gates (50 items x 5) remain outstanding.
scope: The 24 existing self-report items of Väktare v1 only. No item added or removed, no score, key, competency or evidence type changed, no scenario or free-text item touched, no report logic redesigned.
